verses.36:9: Now it happened in the fifth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, in the ninth month, that they proclaimed a fast in the presence of the Lord to all the people in Jerusalem, and to the entire multitude that had streamed together from the cities of Judah into Jerusalem.
verses.36:10: And Baruch read from the scroll the words of Jeremiah in the house of the Lord, in the treasury of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper courtyard, at the entrance of the New Gate of the house of the Lord, in the hearing of all the people.
verses.36:11: And when Micaiah son of Gemariah, son of Shaphan, had heard all the words of the Lord from the book,
verses.36:12: he went down into the king's house, to the treasury of the scribe, and look, all the officials were sitting there: Elishama the scribe, and Delaiah son of Shemaiah, and Elnathan son of Achbor, and Gemariah son of Shaphan, and Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the officials;
verses.36:13: and Micaiah reported to them all the words that he heard as Baruch read from the scroll in the ears of the people.
verses.36:14: Therefore all the officials sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah, son of Shelemiah, son of Cushi, to Baruch, saying, "Take in your hand the scroll from which you read in the hearing of the people, and come." So Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll in his hand and came to them.
verses.36:15: And they said to him, "Sit down and read these things in our ears." And Baruch read in their ears.
verses.36:16: So when they had heard all the words, they were stunned, each one toward his neighbor, and they said to Baruch, "We must report all these words to the king."
verses.36:17: And they questioned him, saying, "Tell us how you wrote all these words from his mouth."
verses.36:18: Then Baruch said to them, "From his mouth he was speaking all these words to me as though reading, and I was writing in the scroll with ink."
verses.36:19: And the officials said to Baruch, "Go and hide yourself, you and Jeremiah, and let no one know where you are."
verses.36:20: And they went in to the king in the court; however, they deposited the scroll in the treasury of Elishama the scribe, and they reported all the words in the hearing of the king.
verses.36:21: And the king sent Jehudi to fetch the scroll; and taking it from the treasury of Elishama the scribe, he read it in the hearing of the king and of all the officials who were standing around the king.
verses.36:22: Now the king was sitting in the winter house, in the ninth month, and a brazier full of burning coals was set before him.
verses.36:23: And when Jehudi had read three or four columns, he cut it with a scribe's knife and threw it into the fire that was on the brazier, until the entire scroll was consumed by the fire that was in the brazier.
verses.36:24: And the king and all his servants who heard all these words were not afraid, nor did they tear their garments.
verses.36:25: Nevertheless, Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah opposed the king so that he would not burn the book, and he did not listen to them.
verses.36:26: And the king commanded Jerahmeel son of Amelech, and Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abdeel, to arrest Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet; but the Lord hid them.
verses.36:27: And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet, after the king had burned the scroll and the words that Baruch had written from the mouth of Jeremiah, saying:
verses.36:28: "Again, take another scroll, and write in it all the former words that were in the first scroll, which Jehoiakim king of Judah burned.
verses.36:29: And to Jehoiakim king of Judah you will say, 'This is what the Lord says: You have burned that scroll, saying, "Why have you written in it, announcing, 'The king of Babylon will swiftly come and lay waste this land, and cause man and beast to cease from it'?"
verses.36:30: Therefore this is what the Lord says against Jehoiakim king of Judah: There will not be anyone from him to sit upon the throne of David, and his corpse will be cast out to the heat by day and to the frost by night.
verses.36:31: And I will visit their iniquities against him, and against his seed, and against his servants; and I will bring upon them, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and upon the men of Judah, all the evil that I spoke to them, and they did not listen.'"
verses.36:32: Then Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch son of Neriah the scribe, who wrote in it from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the book that Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned with fire; and in addition, many more words were added than there had been before.
verses.37:1: And King Zedekiah son of Josiah reigned in place of Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon appointed king in the land of Judah.
verses.37:2: And neither he himself, nor his servants, nor the people of the land obeyed the words of the Lord, which He spoke by the hand of Jeremiah the prophet.
verses.37:3: And King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah, and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest, to Jeremiah the prophet, saying, "Pray for us to the Lord our God."
verses.37:4: Now Jeremiah was walking freely in the midst of the people, for they had not put him into the custody of the prison. Then Pharaoh's army came out from Egypt, and the Chaldeans who were besieging Jerusalem, hearing such a report, withdrew from Jerusalem.
verses.37:5: And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet, saying:
verses.37:6: "This is what the Lord God of Israel says: In this way you will say to the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of Me, 'Look, Pharaoh's army, which came out to your aid, will return to its own land, to Egypt,
verses.37:7: and the Chaldeans will come back and wage war against this city, and capture it, and burn it with fire.'
verses.37:8: This is what the Lord says: Do not deceive your souls, saying, 'Going away, the Chaldeans will depart and withdraw from us,' for they will not depart.
verses.37:9: But even if you strike down the entire army of the Chaldeans who are fighting against you, and some wounded men are left from among them, each one will rise up from his tent and burn this city with fire."
verses.37:10: Therefore, when the army of the Chaldeans had withdrawn from Jerusalem because of Pharaoh's army,
verses.37:11: Jeremiah went out from Jerusalem to go into the land of Benjamin and to divide a possession there in the presence of the citizens.
verses.37:12: And when he had arrived at the Gate of Benjamin, a guard of the gate was there by turns, named Irijah son of Shelemiah, son of Hananiah; and he seized Jeremiah the prophet, saying, "You are deserting to the Chaldeans."
verses.37:13: And Jeremiah answered, "It is false; I am not fleeing to the Chaldeans." Yet he did not listen to him, but Irijah arrested Jeremiah and brought him to the officials.
verses.37:14: Because of this, the officials, angry against Jeremiah, beat him and put him into the prison that was in the house of Jonathan the scribe; for he himself had been set over the prison.
verses.37:15: So Jeremiah entered into the house of the pit and into the dungeon; and Jeremiah stayed there for many days.
verses.37:16: Then King Zedekiah sent and brought him, and he questioned him secretly in his house, and said, "Do you think there is a word from the Lord?" And Jeremiah said, "There is." And he said, "You will be delivered into the hands of the king of Babylon."
verses.37:17: And Jeremiah said to King Zedekiah, "How have I sinned against you, and against your servants, and against your people, that you have put me into the house of the prison?
verses.37:18: Where are your prophets who prophesied to you and said, 'The king of Babylon will not come upon you and upon this land'?
verses.37:19: Now therefore listen, I plead with you, my lord the king: may my plea prevail in your presence, and do not send me back into the house of Jonathan the scribe, so that I do not die there."
verses.37:20: Therefore King Zedekiah commanded that Jeremiah be committed to the courtyard of the prison, and that a loaf of bread be given to him daily, besides stew, until all the loaves from the city were consumed; and Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the prison.
verses.38:1: Now Shephatiah the son of Mattan, and Gedaliah the son of Pashhur, and Jehucal the son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur the son of Malchijah heard the words that Jeremiah was speaking to all the people, saying,
verses.38:2: "This is what the Lord says: 'Whoever remains in this city will die by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence; but whoever flees to the Chaldeans will live, and his soul will be safe and alive.'
verses.38:3: This is what the Lord says: 'This city will surely be handed over into the hand of the army of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it.'"
verses.38:4: And the officials said to the king, "We ask that this man be put to death, for he deliberately weakens the hands of the fighting men who have remained in this city, and the hands of all the people, by speaking to them according to these words; for indeed this man does not seek peace for this people, but harm."
verses.38:5: And King Zedekiah said, "Look, he is in your hands, for it is not right for the king to deny you anything."
verses.38:6: So they took Jeremiah and threw him into the cistern of Malchijah the son of Amelech, which was in the courtyard of the prison; and they lowered Jeremiah by ropes into the cistern, in which there was no water, but mud; and so Jeremiah sank down into the mire.
verses.38:7: Now Ebed-melech the Ethiopian, a eunuch who was in the king's house, heard that they had put Jeremiah into the cistern. Meanwhile, the king was sitting at the Gate of Benjamin.
verses.38:8: And Ebed-melech went out from the king's house and spoke to the king, saying,
verses.38:9: "My lord the king, these men have done wrong in everything they have committed against Jeremiah the prophet, putting him into the cistern so that he may die there of hunger; for there is no longer any bread in the city."
verses.38:10: Then the king commanded Ebed-melech the Ethiopian, saying, "Take thirty men with you from here, and lift Jeremiah the prophet up out of the cistern before he dies."
verses.38:11: So Ebed-melech, taking the men with him, entered the king's house, which was under the storeroom, and took from there old rags and worn-out things that had rotted, and lowered them to Jeremiah into the cistern by cords.
verses.38:12: And Ebed-melech the Ethiopian said to Jeremiah, "Put the old rags and these torn and rotted things under the elbow of your hands and over the ropes." So Jeremiah did this,
verses.38:13: and they pulled Jeremiah up with the ropes and brought him out of the cistern. And Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the prison.
verses.38:14: And King Zedekiah sent and brought Jeremiah the prophet to himself at the third entrance that was in the house of the Lord. And the king said to Jeremiah, "I am asking you a question; do not hide anything from me."
verses.38:15: And Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "If I tell you, will you not kill me? And if I give you counsel, you will not listen to me."
verses.38:16: So King Zedekiah swore to Jeremiah secretly, saying, "As the Lord lives, who made this soul for us, I will not put you to death, nor will I hand you over into the hands of these men who seek your life."
verses.38:17: Then Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "This is what the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, says: 'If you indeed go out to the officials of the king of Babylon, your soul will live, and this city will not be burned with fire; and you and your house will be safe.
verses.38:18: But if you do not go out to the officials of the king of Babylon, this city will be handed over into the hands of the Chaldeans, and they will burn it with fire; and you will not escape from their hand.'"
verses.38:19: And King Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "I am anxious because of the Judeans who have defected to the Chaldeans, for fear that I might be handed over into their hands and they might mock me."
verses.38:20: But Jeremiah answered, "They will not hand you over. Please listen to the voice of the Lord, which I am speaking to you, and it will go well with you, and your soul will live.
verses.38:21: But if you refuse to go out, this is the word that the Lord has shown me:
verses.38:22: Look, all the women who have remained in the house of the king of Judah will be brought out to the officials of the king of Babylon, and they themselves will say, 'Your men of peace have misled you and prevailed against you; they have sunk your feet into the mire and into a slippery place, and have withdrawn from you.'
verses.38:23: And all your wives and your sons will be brought out to the Chaldeans, and you will not escape their hands, but you will be captured by the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will burn this city with fire."
verses.38:24: Then Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "Let no one know these words, and you will not die.
verses.38:25: But if the officials hear that I have spoken with you, and they come to you and say to you, 'Tell us what you spoke with the king; do not hide it from us, and we will not kill you; and what did the king speak with you?'
verses.38:26: then you will say to them, 'I laid down my pleas before the king, that he would not order me to be brought back into the house of Jonathan to die there.'"
verses.38:27: So all the officials came to Jeremiah and questioned him, and he spoke to them according to all the words that the king had commanded him. And they left him alone, for nothing had been heard.
verses.38:28: And Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the prison until the day on which Jerusalem was captured; and it came about that Jerusalem was captured.
verses.39:1: In the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his army came to Jerusalem and besieged it.
verses.39:2: And in the eleventh year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, on the fifth day of the month, the city was broken open,
verses.39:3: and all the officials of the king of Babylon entered and sat in the Middle Gate: Nergal, Sharezer, Samgar-nebo, Sarsechim, Rab-saris, Nergal, Sharezer, Rab-mag, and all the rest of the officials of the king of Babylon.
verses.39:4: And when Zedekiah king of Judah and all the men of war saw them, they fled; and they went out of the city by night by the way of the king's garden and through the gate that was between the two walls, and they went out toward the way of the wilderness.
verses.39:5: But the army of the Chaldeans pursued them, and they captured Zedekiah in the plain of the wilderness of Jericho; and having captured him, they brought him to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, at Riblah, which is in the land of Hamath, and he spoke judgments to him.
verses.39:6: And the king of Babylon killed the sons of Zedekiah at Riblah before his eyes; and the king of Babylon killed all the nobles of Judah.
verses.39:7: He also gouged out the eyes of Zedekiah and bound him with shackles so that he might be led to Babylon.
verses.39:8: The Chaldeans also set fire to the king's house and the house of the common people, and they tore down the wall of Jerusalem.
verses.39:9: And the remnant of the people who had remained in the city, and the deserters who had defected to him, and the rest of the common people who had remained, Nebuzaradan the captain of the troops carried away into Babylon.
verses.39:10: And some of the poor among the common people, who had nothing at all, Nebuzaradan the captain of the troops left behind in the land of Judah, and he gave them vineyards and cisterns on that day.
verses.39:11: Now Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had given orders concerning Jeremiah to Nebuzaradan the captain of the troops, saying,
verses.39:12: "Take him and set your eyes upon him, and do him no harm; rather, just as he wishes, so do for him."
verses.39:13: Therefore Nebuzaradan the commander of the troops sent, along with Nebushazban, and Rab-saris, and Nergal, and Sharezer, and Rab-mag, and all the nobles of the king of Babylon;
verses.39:14: they sent and took Jeremiah from the courtyard of the prison, and handed him over to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, so that he might go into the house and live among the people.
verses.39:15: Now the word of the Lord had come to Jeremiah while he was confined in the courtyard of the prison, saying,
verses.39:16: "Go and speak to Ebed-melech the Ethiopian, saying, 'This is what the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Look, I will bring My words upon this city for harm and not for good, and they will be before your sight on that day.
verses.39:17: And I will deliver you on that day, says the Lord, and you will not be handed over into the hands of the men whom you dread;
verses.39:18: but rescuing you, I will deliver you, and you will not fall by the sword; rather, your soul will be yours for safety, because you have had confidence in Me, says the Lord.'"
verses.40:1: The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord after he was released from Ramah by Nebuzaradan, the captain of the troops, when he took him bound in chains among all those who were going into exile from Jerusalem and Judah and were being led to Babylon.
verses.40:2: So the commander of the troops took Jeremiah and said to him, "The Lord your God spoke this disaster against this place,
verses.40:3: and the Lord has brought it about and done just as He spoke, because you sinned against the Lord and did not listen to His voice; and this word has come about for you.
verses.40:4: Now therefore, look, I have released you today from the chains that are on your hands. If it pleases you to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will set my eyes upon you; but if it displeases you to come with me to Babylon, stay behind. Look, the whole land is before you; whatever you choose, and wherever it pleases you to go, proceed there,
verses.40:5: and do not come with me, but live with Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has appointed over the cities of Judah; live therefore with him among the people, or wherever it pleases you to go, go." The captain of the troops also gave him provisions and small gifts, and let him go.
verses.40:6: So Jeremiah came to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam at Mizpah, and lived with him among the people who had been left in the land.
verses.40:7: And when all the commanders of the army who had been scattered throughout the regions, they and their associates, heard that the king of Babylon had put Gedaliah the son of Ahikam in charge of the land, and that he had entrusted to him men, women, and little children, and some of the poor of the land who had not been carried away to Babylon,
verses.40:8: they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and Johanan and Jonathan the sons of Kareah, and Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth, and the sons of Ephai, who were from Netophathi, and Jezaniah the son of Maacathi, they and their men.
verses.40:9: And Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, swore to them and to their companions, saying, "Do not be afraid to serve the Chaldeans; live in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well with you.
verses.40:10: Look, as for me, I am living in Mizpah so that I may answer the command of the Chaldeans who are sent to us; but as for you, gather the vintage, and the harvest, and the oil, and store them in your vessels, and remain in your cities that you hold."
verses.40:11: Moreover, all the Judeans who were in Moab, and among the sons of Ammon, and in Idumea, and in all the regions, when they heard that the king of Babylon had granted a remnant in Judea and that he had appointed Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, over them,
verses.40:12: returned, I say, all the Judeans, from all the places to which they had fled, and came into the land of Judah, to Gedaliah at Mizpah, and gathered wine and a very great harvest.
verses.40:13: Now Johanan the son of Kareah and all the commanders of the army who had been scattered in the regions came to Gedaliah at Mizpah,
verses.40:14: and said to him, "Know that Baalis, king of the sons of Ammon, has sent Ishmael the son of Nethaniah to strike down your life." But Gedaliah the son of Ahikam did not believe them.
verses.40:15: Then Johanan the son of Kareah spoke to Gedaliah privately in Mizpah, saying, "I will go and strike down Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, with no one knowing, so that he does not destroy your life, and all the Judeans who have been gathered to you are not scattered, and the remnant of Judah does not perish."
verses.40:16: And Gedaliah the son of Ahikam said to Johanan the son of Kareah, "Do not do this thing, for you are speaking a falsehood about Ishmael."
verses.41:1: And it happened in the seventh month that Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, of the royal seed, and the nobles of the king, and ten men with him, came to Gedaliah son of Ahikam in Mizpah, and they ate bread there together in Mizpah.
verses.41:2: Then Ishmael son of Nethaniah rose up, and the ten men who were with him, and they struck Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, with the sword, and killed the one whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.
verses.41:3: Ishmael also struck down all the Jews who were with Gedaliah in Mizpah, and the Chaldeans who were found there, and the fighting men.
verses.41:4: Now on the second day after he had killed Gedaliah, while no one yet knew,
verses.41:5: men came from Shechem, and from Shiloh, and from Samaria, eighty men, with their beards shaved, and with their garments torn, and disheveled; and they had offerings and frankincense in their hand to offer in the house of the Lord.
verses.41:6: So Ishmael son of Nethaniah went out from Mizpah to meet them, walking along and weeping as he went; and when he had met them, he said to them, "Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam."
verses.41:7: And when they had come to the middle of the city, Ishmael son of Nethaniah killed them near the middle of the cistern, he and the men who were with him.
verses.41:8: But ten men were found among them who said to Ishmael, "Do not kill us, for we have treasures in the field, of wheat, and of barley, and of oil, and of honey." And he stopped, and did not kill them with their brothers.
verses.41:9: Now the cistern into which Ishmael had thrown all the corpses of the men whom he struck down because of Gedaliah is the very one that King Asa made because of Baasha king of Israel; Ishmael son of Nethaniah filled it with those who were killed.
verses.41:10: And Ishmael led captive all the remnant of the people who were in Mizpah, the daughters of the king, and all the people who had remained in Mizpah, whom Nebuzaradan, commander of the troops, had entrusted to Gedaliah son of Ahikam; and Ishmael son of Nethaniah captured them and departed to cross over to the sons of Ammon.
verses.41:11: Now Johanan son of Kareah, and all the commanders of the fighting men who were with him, heard of all the evil that Ishmael son of Nethaniah had done,
verses.41:12: and having taken all the men, they set out to fight against Ishmael son of Nethaniah; and they found him by the many waters that are in Gibeon.
verses.41:13: And when all the people who were with Ishmael saw Johanan son of Kareah, and all the commanders of the fighting men who were with him, they rejoiced,
verses.41:14: and all the people whom Ishmael had captured in Mizpah turned around, and turning back, went to Johanan son of Kareah.
verses.41:15: But Ishmael son of Nethaniah fled with eight men from before Johanan, and went to the sons of Ammon.
verses.41:16: So Johanan son of Kareah, and all the commanders of the fighting men who were with him, took all the remnant of the common people whom he had brought back from Ishmael son of Nethaniah from Mizpah, after he struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam: men strong for battle, and women, and children, and eunuchs, whom he had brought back from Gibeon.
verses.41:17: And they departed and stayed, sojourning in Chimham, which is near Bethlehem, to go on and enter Egypt,
verses.41:18: from before the Chaldeans; for they were afraid of them, because Ishmael son of Nethaniah had struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had placed in charge in the land of Judah.
verses.42:1: And all the commanders of the fighting men, and Johanan son of Kareah, and Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and the rest of the common people, from the small to the great, came near,
verses.42:2: and said to Jeremiah the prophet, "Let our petition fall in your sight, and pray for us to the Lord your God, for all this remnant, for we are left few out of many, just as your eyes look upon us;
verses.42:3: and may the Lord your God declare to us the way by which we should go, and the thing that we should do."
verses.42:4: Then Jeremiah the prophet said to them, "I have heard. Look, I am praying to the Lord your God according to your words; every word, whatever He answers me, I will make known to you, and I will not conceal anything from you."
verses.42:5: And they said to Jeremiah, "May the Lord be a witness of truth and faithfulness between us, if we do not act so according to every word with which the Lord your God sends you to us;
verses.42:6: whether it is good or bad, we will obey the voice of the Lord our God, to whom we are sending you, so that it may go well with us when we listen to the voice of the Lord our God."
verses.42:7: Now when ten days had been completed, the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah,
verses.42:8: and he called Johanan son of Kareah, and all the commanders of the fighting men who were with him, and all the people, from the least to the great.
verses.42:9: And he said to them, "This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says, to whom you sent me to lay down your petitions in His sight:
verses.42:10: 'If you remain quietly in this land, I will build you up and not tear down; I will plant and not uproot; for I have already been appeased over the calamity that I have done to you.
verses.42:11: Do not be afraid before the king of Babylon, whom you dread in terror; do not fear him, says the Lord, for I am with you to save you and to deliver you from his hand;
verses.42:12: and I will grant you mercies, and I will have mercy on you, and I will make you dwell in your land.'
verses.42:13: But if you say, 'We will not dwell in this land, nor will we listen to the voice of the Lord our God,'
verses.42:14: saying, 'By no means, but we will go to the land of Egypt, where we will not see war, and we will not hear the blast of the trumpet, and we will not endure famine, and there we will dwell,'
verses.42:15: because of this, now hear the word of the Lord, remnant of Judah. This is what the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, says: 'If you set your face to enter Egypt, and go in to dwell there,
verses.42:16: the sword that you dread will overtake you there in the land of Egypt; and the famine about which you are anxious will cling to you in Egypt, and there you will die.
verses.42:17: And all the men who have set their face to enter Egypt, to dwell there, will die by the sword, and by famine, and by pestilence; none of them will remain or escape from before the calamity that I will bring upon them.'
verses.42:18: For this is what the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, says: 'Just as My fury and My indignation were kindled upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so My indignation will be kindled upon you when you have entered Egypt; and you will become an oath, and an astonishment, and a curse, and a reproach, and you will never again see this place.'
verses.42:19: The word of the Lord is upon you, remnant of Judah: 'Do not enter Egypt.' You will surely know that I have solemnly warned you today,
verses.42:20: because you have deceived your own souls. For you sent me to the Lord our God, saying, 'Pray for us to the Lord our God, and according to everything that the Lord our God says to you, declare it so to us, and we will do it.'
verses.42:21: And I have declared it to you today, and you have not listened to the voice of the Lord your God concerning all things for which He sent me to you.
verses.42:22: Now therefore you will surely know that by the sword, and by famine, and by pestilence you will die in the place into which you desired to enter, to dwell there."
verses.43:1: Now it happened, when Jeremiah had finished speaking to the people all the words of the Lord their God, for which the Lord their God had sent him to them, all these words,
verses.43:2: that Azariah son of Hoshaiah, and Johanan son of Kareah, and all the arrogant men spoke, saying to Jeremiah, "You are speaking a lie: the Lord our God has not sent you, saying, 'Do not enter Egypt to dwell there.'
verses.43:3: But Baruch son of Neriah is inciting you against us, to hand us over into the hands of the Chaldeans, to kill us and cause us to be carried away into Babylon."
verses.43:4: And Johanan son of Kareah, and all the commanders of the fighting men, and all the people did not listen to the voice of the Lord, to remain in the land of Judah.
verses.43:5: But Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the fighting men took all of the remnant of Judah who had returned from all the nations to which they had previously been scattered, to dwell in the land of Judah:
verses.43:6: the men, and the women, and the little ones, and the daughters of the king, and every soul whom Nebuzaradan, commander of the troops, had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, and Jeremiah the prophet, and Baruch son of Neriah;
verses.43:7: and they entered the land of Egypt, because they did not obey the voice of the Lord, and they came as far as Tahpanhes.
verses.43:8: And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes, saying,
verses.43:9: "Take large stones in your hand, and hide them in the vault that is beneath the brick wall at the gate of the house of Pharaoh in Tahpanhes, while the Jewish men look on,
verses.43:10: and say to them, 'This is what the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Look, I will send and take Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, My servant; and I will set his throne upon these stones that I have hidden, and he will establish his royal seat upon them;
verses.43:11: and he will come and strike the land of Egypt: those for death, to death; and those for captivity, to captivity; and those for the sword, to the sword;
verses.43:12: and he will kindle a fire in the shrines of the gods of Egypt, and he will burn them and lead them captive; and he will wrap himself with the land of Egypt just as a shepherd wraps himself with his cloak, and he will go out from there in peace;
verses.43:13: and he will shatter the statues of the house of the sun that are in the land of Egypt, and he will burn the shrines of the gods of Egypt with fire.'"
verses.44:1: The word that came through Jeremiah to all the Jews who were living in the land of Egypt, living in Migdol, and in Tahpanhes, and in Memphis, and in the land of Pathros, saying:
verses.44:2: "This is what the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, says: You have seen all this evil that I have brought upon Jerusalem and upon all the cities of Judah; and look, they are deserted today, and there is no inhabitant in them,
verses.44:3: because of the wickedness that they did to provoke Me to anger, going to sacrifice and to worship foreign gods whom they did not know—neither they, nor you, nor your fathers.
verses.44:4: And I sent to you all My servants the prophets, rising in the night, sending and saying, 'Do not do an abominable thing of this kind, which I hate.'
verses.44:5: And they did not listen, nor did they incline their ear to turn from their evils and not sacrifice to foreign gods.
verses.44:6: And My indignation and My fury flared up and were kindled in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem, and they have been turned into a wasteland and a devastation, as on this day.
verses.44:7: And now this is what the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Why are you doing this great evil against your own souls, so that man and woman, little child and nursing infant perish from among you, from the midst of Judah, and nothing remaining is left to you,
verses.44:8: provoking Me with the works of your hands, by sacrificing to foreign gods in the land of Egypt, into which you have entered to live there, so that you perish and become a curse and a reproach to all the nations of the earth?
verses.44:9: Have you forgotten the evils of your fathers, and the evils of the kings of Judah, and the evils of his wives, and your own evils, and the evils of your wives, which they did in the land of Judah and in the regions of Jerusalem?
verses.44:10: They have not been cleansed to this day, and they have not feared, and they have not walked in the law of the Lord and in My precepts, which I set before you and before your fathers.
verses.44:11: Therefore this is what the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Look, I will set My face against you for evil, and I will destroy all Judah.
verses.44:12: And I will take the remnant of Judah who have set their faces to enter the land of Egypt and live there, and they will all be consumed in the land of Egypt; they will fall by the sword and by famine, and they will be consumed from the least to the greatest; by the sword and by famine they will die, and they will become an oath, and a wonder, and a curse, and a reproach.
verses.44:13: And I will punish the inhabitants of the land of Egypt just as I punished Jerusalem, with sword, and famine, and plague;
verses.44:14: and there will be no one who escapes or remains from the remnant of the Jews who go to sojourn in the land of Egypt and to return to the land of Judah, toward which they lift up their souls to return and live there; they will not return, except those who have escaped."
verses.44:15: Then all the men who knew that their wives were sacrificing to foreign gods, and all the women, of whom a great multitude was standing there, and all the people living in the land of Egypt in Pathros, answered Jeremiah, saying:
verses.44:16: "As for the word that you have spoken to us in the name of the Lord, we will not listen to it from you;
verses.44:17: but we will surely do every word that will go out from our mouth, to sacrifice to the queen of heaven and to pour out libations to her, just as we and our fathers, our kings and our princes did in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem; and we were filled with bread, and it went well with us, and we saw no evil.
verses.44:18: But from the time when we ceased sacrificing to the queen of heaven and pouring out libations to her, we lack everything, and we have been consumed by sword and by famine.
verses.44:19: And if we sacrifice to the queen of heaven and pour out libations to her, did we make cakes for her to worship her and pour out libations to her without our husbands?"
verses.44:20: And Jeremiah said to all the people—against the men, and against the women, and against the whole populace—who had answered him a word, saying:
verses.44:21: "The sacrifice that you sacrificed in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem—you and your fathers, your kings and your princes, and the people of the land—did the Lord not remember these things, and did it not come up upon His heart?
verses.44:22: And the Lord could no longer bear it because of the wickedness of your pursuits and because of the abominations that you committed; and your land has become a desolation, and an astonishment, and a curse, because there is no inhabitant, as it is this day.
verses.44:23: Because you sacrificed to idols, and sinned against the Lord, and did not listen to the voice of the Lord, and did not walk in His law, and in His precepts, and in His testimonies, therefore these evils have come upon you, as it is this day."
verses.44:24: Then Jeremiah said to all the people and to all the women, "Hear the word of the Lord, all Judah who are in the land of Egypt.
verses.44:25: This is what the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, says: You and your wives have spoken with your mouth, and with your hands you have fulfilled it, saying, 'Let us perform our vows that we have vowed, to sacrifice to the queen of heaven and to pour out libations to her.' You have fulfilled your vows, and in deed you have carried them out.
verses.44:26: Therefore hear the word of the Lord, all Judah who live in the land of Egypt: Look, I have sworn by My great name, says the Lord, that My name will by no means any longer be called upon from the mouth of any Jewish man saying, 'The Lord God lives,' in all the land of Egypt.
verses.44:27: Look, I will watch over them for evil and not for good; and all the men of Judah who are in the land of Egypt will be consumed by sword and by famine, until they are completely consumed.
verses.44:28: And those who escape the sword will return from the land of Egypt to the land of Judah, a few men; and all the remnant of Judah, of those entering the land of Egypt to live there, will know whose word will be fulfilled, Mine or theirs.
verses.44:29: And this is a sign to you, says the Lord, that I will punish you in this place, so that you may know that My words will truly be fulfilled against you for evil:
verses.44:30: This is what the Lord says: Look, I will hand over Pharaoh Hophra, king of Egypt, into the hand of his enemies and into the hand of those seeking his life, just as I handed over Zedekiah, king of Judah, into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, his enemy and the one seeking his life."
verses.45:1: The word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch the son of Neriah, when he had written these words in a book from the mouth of Jeremiah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah, saying:
verses.45:2: "This is what the Lord God of Israel says to you, Baruch:
verses.45:3: You have said, 'Woe to wretched me! For the Lord has added sorrow to my sorrow; I have toiled in my groaning, and I have not found rest.'
verses.45:4: This is what the Lord says: This is what you will say to him, 'Look, those whom I have built I am tearing down, and those whom I have planted I am uprooting, and this whole land;
verses.45:5: and are you seeking great things for yourself? Do not seek them, for look, I will bring evil upon all flesh, says the Lord, and I will give you your life for safety in all the places to which you may go.'"
verses.46:1: The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah the prophet against the nations.
verses.46:2: Concerning Egypt, against the army of Pharaoh Necho king of Egypt, which was by the river Euphrates at Carchemish, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah.
verses.46:3: "Prepare shield and buckler, and advance to war.
verses.46:4: Harness the horses, and mount, horsemen; stand in helmets, polish the spears, clothe yourselves in coats of mail.
verses.46:5: What then? I saw them terrified and turning their backs, their mighty men cut down; they fled in haste and did not look back. Terror on every side," says the Lord.
verses.46:6: Let the swift not flee, nor let the mighty one think himself saved; in the north, by the river Euphrates, they have been conquered and have fallen.
verses.46:7: Who is this who rises like a river, and whose surging waters swell like those of rivers?
verses.46:8: Egypt rises like a river, and like rivers her waves will be tossed; and she will say, "Rising, I will cover the earth; I will destroy the city and its inhabitants."
verses.46:9: Mount the horses, and exult in chariots, and let the mighty men advance: Ethiopia and the Libyans holding the shield, and the Lydians seizing and shooting arrows.
verses.46:10: But that day of the Lord God of hosts is a day of vengeance, so that He may exact retribution from His enemies; the sword will devour and be satisfied, and it will be made drunk with their blood; for there is a sacrifice of the Lord God of hosts in the land of the north, by the river Euphrates.
verses.46:11: Go up to Gilead and take resin, virgin daughter of Egypt; in vain you multiply remedies; there will be no healing for you.
verses.46:12: The nations have heard of your disgrace, and your wailing has filled the earth; for mighty man has struck against mighty man, and both have fallen together.
verses.46:13: The word which the Lord spoke to Jeremiah the prophet, concerning the fact that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon was about to come and strike the land of Egypt:
verses.46:14: "Declare to Egypt, and make it heard in Migdol, and let it resound in Memphis and in Tahpanhes; say, 'Stand and prepare yourself, for the sword will devour the things that are around you.'
verses.46:15: Why has your mighty one rotted away? He did not stand, because the Lord has overthrown him.
verses.46:16: He has multiplied those who fall, and a man has fallen against his neighbor, and they will say, 'Arise, and let us return to our people and to the land of our birth, from the face of the sword of the dove.'
verses.46:17: Call the name of Pharaoh king of Egypt, 'Time has brought tumult.'
verses.46:18: As I live," says the King (the Lord of hosts is His name), "surely like Tabor among the mountains, and like Carmel by the sea, he will come.
verses.46:19: Make for yourself baggage for exile, inhabitant, daughter of Egypt; for Memphis will become a desolation, and will be deserted, and will be uninhabitable.
verses.46:20: Egypt is a graceful and beautiful heifer; a goader from the north will come to her.
verses.46:21: Her mercenaries also, who lived in her midst like fattened calves, have turned and fled together, and could not stand; for the day of their slaughter has come upon them, the time of their visitation.
verses.46:22: Her voice will sound like bronze, for they will hasten with an army, and with axes they will come against her like those cutting wood.
verses.46:23: They have cut down her forest," says the Lord, "which cannot be counted; they have multiplied beyond locusts, and there is no number to them.
verses.46:24: The daughter of Egypt has been put to shame, and handed over into the hand of the people of the north."
verses.46:25: The Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, has said: "Look, I will visit upon the tumult of Alexandria, and upon Pharaoh, and upon Egypt, and upon her gods, and upon her kings, and upon Pharaoh, and upon those who trust in him.
verses.46:26: And I will give them into the hand of those who seek their life, and into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and into the hand of his servants; and after these things it will be inhabited as in former days, says the Lord.
verses.46:27: And you, do not fear, My servant Jacob, and do not be dismayed, Israel; for look, I will save you from afar, and your seed from the land of your captivity; and Jacob will return, and will rest, and will prosper, and there will be no one to terrify him.
verses.46:28: And you, do not fear, My servant Jacob," says the Lord, "for I am with you; for I will consume all the nations to which I have driven you out, yet I will not consume you; but I will discipline you in justice, and I will not spare you as if innocent."
verses.47:1: The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah the prophet against the Philistines, before Pharaoh struck Gaza.
verses.47:2: This is what the Lord says: "Look, waters are rising from the north, and they will be like an overflowing torrent, and they will cover the land and its fullness, the city and its inhabitants. People will cry out, and all the inhabitants of the land will wail,
verses.47:3: at the noise of the pomp of arms and of his warriors, at the commotion of his chariots and the multitude of his wheels. Fathers did not look back to their children, with hands grown limp,
verses.47:4: because of the coming of the day on which all the Philistines will be laid waste, and Tyre and Sidon will be shattered along with all their remaining helpers; for the Lord has ravaged the Philistines, the remnant of the island of Cappadocia.
verses.47:5: Baldness has come upon Gaza; Ashkelon has fallen silent, and the remnant of their valley: how long will you gash yourself?
verses.47:6: Sword of the Lord, how long will you not rest? Enter into your sheath, grow cool, and be silent.
verses.47:7: How will it rest, since the Lord has commanded it against Ashkelon and against its coastal regions, and has appointed it there?"
verses.48:1: Concerning Moab. This is what the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, says: "Woe upon Nebo, for it has been laid waste and put to shame! Kiriathaim has been captured; the strong one has been put to shame and has trembled.
verses.48:2: There is no longer exultation in Moab against Heshbon; they have plotted evil: 'Come, and let us wipe her out from being a nation.' Therefore in silence you will fall silent, and the sword will follow you.
verses.48:3: The sound of an outcry from Horonaim: devastation and great shattering!
verses.48:4: Moab has been shattered; proclaim the outcry to her little ones.
verses.48:5: For by the ascent of Luhith she will go up weeping in tears, for on the descent of Horonaim the enemies have heard the wailing of shattering.
verses.48:6: Flee, save your lives, and you will be like tamarisks in the desert;
verses.48:7: for because you have had confidence in your strongholds and in your treasures, you also will be captured; and Chemosh will go into exile, his priests and his princes together.
verses.48:8: And the plunderer will come upon every city, and no city will be saved; and the valleys will perish, and the plains will be ruined, for the Lord has spoken.
verses.48:9: Give a flower to Moab, for blossoming she will go forth; and her cities will be deserted and uninhabitable.
verses.48:10: Cursed is the one who does the work of the Lord deceitfully, and cursed is the one who holds back his sword from blood.
verses.48:11: Moab has been fertile from his youth, and has rested on his dregs; nor has he been poured from vessel to vessel, and he has not gone into exile; therefore his taste has remained in him, and his aroma has not been changed.
verses.48:12: Therefore look, the days are coming," says the Lord, "and I will send to him arrangers and tilters of wine flasks, and they will tip him over, and empty his vessels, and smash their flasks.
verses.48:13: And Moab will be put to shame by Chemosh, just as the house of Israel was put to shame by Bethel, in which it had confidence.
verses.48:14: How do you say, 'We are strong, and mighty men for battle'?
verses.48:15: Moab has been laid waste, and her cities have collapsed, and her chosen young men have gone down to the slaughter," says the King; the Lord of hosts is His name.
verses.48:16: The ruin of Moab is close to coming, and his calamity will rush on very swiftly.
verses.48:17: Console him, all you who are around him; and all you who know his name, say, "How has the strong rod been broken, the glorious staff?"
verses.48:18: Come down from glory and sit in thirst, dwelling of the daughter of Dibon, for the destroyer of Moab has come up against you; he has ruined your strongholds.
verses.48:19: Stand by the road and watch, dwelling of Aroer; question the one who is fleeing, and to the one who has escaped say, "What has happened?"
verses.48:20: Moab has been put to shame, for he has been conquered. Wail and cry out; proclaim in Arnon that Moab has been laid waste,
verses.48:21: and judgment has come to the land of the plain, upon Holon, and upon Jahaz, and upon Mephaath,
verses.48:22: and upon Dibon, and upon Nebo, and upon the house of Diblathaim,
verses.48:23: and upon Kiriathaim, and upon Beth-gamul, and upon Beth-meon,
verses.48:24: and upon Kerioth, and upon Bozrah, and upon all the cities of the land of Moab, those that are far and those that are near.
verses.48:25: "The horn of Moab has been cut off, and his arm has been shattered," says the Lord.
verses.48:26: Make him drunk, because he has raised himself up against the Lord; and Moab will strike his hand in his vomit, and he himself also will become an object of derision.
verses.48:27: For Israel was an object of derision to you, as if you had found him among thieves; therefore, because of your words that you have spoken against him, you will be led away captive.
verses.48:28: Leave the cities and dwell in the rock, inhabitants of Moab, and be like a dove nesting at the top of the mouth of a cleft.
verses.48:29: We have heard of the pride of Moab; he is exceedingly proud: his loftiness, and arrogance, and pride, and the haughtiness of his heart.
verses.48:30: "I know," says the Lord, "his boasting, and that his strength is not in proportion to it, nor has it attempted to act according to what it was able.
verses.48:31: Therefore I will wail over Moab, and to all Moab I will cry out, to the lamenting men of the clay wall;
verses.48:32: with the mourning of Jazer I will weep for you, vine of Sibmah. Your shoots have crossed the sea; they have reached as far as the sea of Jazer; upon your harvest and your vintage the plunderer has rushed.
verses.48:33: Gladness and exultation have been taken away from Carmel and from the land of Moab, and I have removed the wine from the winepresses; by no means will the treader of the grape sing the accustomed chant.
verses.48:34: From the outcry of Heshbon as far as Elealeh and Jahaz they have raised their voice; from Zoar as far as Horonaim, like a three-year-old heifer; the waters of Nimrim also will be very bad.
verses.48:35: And I will remove from Moab," says the Lord, "the one who offers on the high places and who sacrifices to his gods.
verses.48:36: Therefore My heart will resound like flutes for Moab, and My heart will give the sound of flutes for the men of the clay wall; because he did more than he could, therefore they have perished.
verses.48:37: For every head will be baldness, and every beard will be shaved; on all hands there will be binding, and upon every back, sackcloth;
verses.48:38: upon all the rooftops of Moab and in its squares, all is mourning; for I have shattered Moab like a useless vessel," says the Lord.
verses.48:39: How has she been conquered, and they have wailed? How has Moab lowered his neck and been put to shame? And Moab will become an object of derision and an example to all those around him.
verses.48:40: This is what the Lord says: "Look, like an eagle he will fly and will spread out his wings against Moab.
verses.48:41: Kerioth has been captured, and the strongholds have been seized; and the heart of the mighty men of Moab on that day will be like the heart of a woman in labor,
verses.48:42: and Moab will cease to be a people, because he has boasted against the Lord.
verses.48:43: Terror and pit and snare are upon you, inhabitant of Moab," says the Lord.
verses.48:44: "Whoever flees from the face of terror will fall into the pit, and whoever climbs up out of the pit will be caught in the snare; for I will bring upon Moab the year of their visitation," says the Lord.
verses.48:45: In the shadow of Heshbon stood those fleeing from the snare, because a fire has gone out from Heshbon and a flame from the midst of Sihon; and it will devour part of Moab and the crown of the head of the sons of tumult.
verses.48:46: Woe to you, Moab: you have perished, people of Chemosh, because your sons and your daughters have been taken into captivity.
verses.48:47: And I will turn back the captivity of Moab in the last days, says the Lord. Up to this point are the judgments of Moab.
verses.49:1: Concerning the sons of Ammon. This is what the Lord says: "Does Israel have no sons, or does he have no heir? Why then has Milcom possessed Gad by inheritance, and his people dwelt in its cities?
verses.49:2: Therefore, look, days are coming," says the Lord, "and I will cause the roar of battle to be heard over Rabbah of the sons of Ammon, and she will be shattered into tumult, and her daughters will be burned with fire, and Israel will possess his possessors," says the Lord.
verses.49:3: "Wail, Heshbon, for Ai has been laid waste; cry out, daughters of Rabbah: wrap yourselves in sackcloth, lament and go around among the hedges, for Milcom will be led into exile, his priests and his princes together.
verses.49:4: Why do you boast in the valleys? Your valley has flowed away, delicate daughter, who trusted in your treasures and said, 'Who will come to me?'
verses.49:5: Look, I will bring terror upon you," says the Lord God of hosts, "from all who are around you; and you will be scattered, each one away from your sight, and there will be no one to gather those who flee."
verses.49:6: "And after these things I will cause the captives of the sons of Ammon to return," says the Lord.
verses.49:7: Concerning Idumea. This is what the Lord of hosts says: "Is there no longer wisdom in Teman? Counsel has perished from the sons; their wisdom has become useless.
verses.49:8: Flee, and turn your backs; go down into the chasm, inhabitants of Dedan, for I have brought the destruction of Esau upon him, the time of his visitation.
verses.49:9: If grape-gatherers had come upon you, they would not have left a cluster; if thieves by night, they would have seized what was enough for themselves.
verses.49:10: But I have uncovered Esau; I have revealed his hidden places, and he will not be able to be concealed. His seed has been laid waste, as well as his brothers and his neighbors, and he will be no more.
verses.49:11: Leave your orphans; I will make them live, and your widows will hope in Me."
verses.49:12: For this is what the Lord says: "Look, those whose judgment was not to drink the cup will certainly drink; and you, will you be left as though innocent? You will not be innocent, but you will certainly drink.
verses.49:13: For by Myself I have sworn," says the Lord, "that Bozrah will become a desolation, and a reproach, and a wasteland, and a curse, and all its cities will become everlasting desolations."
verses.49:14: I have heard a report from the Lord, and an envoy has been sent to the nations: "Gather together, and come against it, and let us rise up for battle."
verses.49:15: "For look, I have made you small among the nations, contemptible among people.
verses.49:16: Your arrogance has deceived you, and the pride of your heart, you who dwell in the caverns of the rock and strive to grasp the height of the hill; though you lift your nest high like an eagle, from there I will bring you down," says the Lord.
verses.49:17: "And Idumea will become deserted; everyone who passes through it will be astonished and will hiss over all its wounds.
verses.49:18: Just as Sodom and Gomorrah and its neighboring towns were overthrown," says the Lord, "no man will dwell there, and no son of man will inhabit it.
verses.49:19: Look, like a lion he will come up from the pride of the Jordan to the strong beauty, for suddenly I will make him run to her. And who will be the chosen one whom I will appoint over her? For who is like Me? And who will withstand Me? And who is this shepherd who can resist My face?"
verses.49:20: Therefore hear the counsel of the Lord that He has formed concerning Edom, and His plans that He has devised concerning the inhabitants of Teman: surely the little ones of the flock will cast them down; surely they will shatter their dwelling with them.
verses.49:21: At the sound of their downfall the earth shook; the cry of its voice was heard at the Red Sea.
verses.49:22: Look, like an eagle he will rise up and fly away, and spread out his wings over Bozrah; and the heart of the mighty men of Idumea in that day will be like the heart of a woman in labor.
verses.49:23: Concerning Damascus. Hamath and Arpad are confounded, for they have heard a most evil report; they are troubled on the sea; because of anxiety it could not rest.
verses.49:24: Damascus has grown feeble, she has turned to flight; trembling has seized her, anguish and pangs have taken hold of her like a woman in labor.
verses.49:25: How have they abandoned the praiseworthy city, the city of joy?
verses.49:26: "Therefore her young men will fall in her squares, and all the men of battle will fall silent in that day," says the Lord of hosts.
verses.49:27: "And I will kindle a fire in the wall of Damascus, and it will devour the fortifications of Ben-hadad."
verses.49:28: Concerning Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck. This is what the Lord says: "Arise, and go up against Kedar, and lay waste the sons of the east.
verses.49:29: They will seize their tents and their flocks; they will carry off for themselves their hides, and all their vessels, and their camels, and they will proclaim dread over them all around.
verses.49:30: Flee, depart hastily, stay in the chasms, you who dwell in Hazor," says the Lord, "for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has formed a counsel against you and has devised plans against you.
verses.49:31: Rise up, and go up against a quiet nation, and one dwelling confidently," says the Lord. "They have neither doors nor bars; they dwell alone.
verses.49:32: And their camels will become plunder, and the multitude of livestock a prey; and I will scatter them to every wind, those who have their hair clipped, and from every border of theirs I will bring ruin upon them," says the Lord.
verses.49:33: "And Hazor will become a dwelling place of dragons, deserted forever; no man will remain there, nor will a son of man inhabit it."
verses.49:34: The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah the prophet against Elam, in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, saying:
verses.49:35: "This is what the Lord of hosts says: Look, I will break the bow of Elam, and their foremost strength;
verses.49:36: and I will bring upon Elam four winds from the four quarters of heaven, and I will scatter them into all these winds, and there will not be a nation to which the fugitives of Elam do not come.
verses.49:37: And I will make Elam terrified before their enemies and in the sight of those who seek their life; and I will bring calamity upon them, the anger of My fury," says the Lord, "and I will send the sword after them until I consume them.
verses.49:38: And I will set My throne in Elam, and I will destroy kings and princes from there," says the Lord.
verses.49:39: "Yet in the last days I will cause the captives of Elam to return," says the Lord.
verses.50:1: The word which the Lord spoke concerning Babylon and concerning the land of the Chaldeans, by the hand of Jeremiah the prophet:
verses.50:2: "Declare among the nations, and make it heard; lift up a standard, proclaim, and do not conceal it; say, 'Babylon has been captured, Bel has been put to shame, Merodach has been conquered, her carved images have been put to shame, their idols have been overcome.'
verses.50:3: For a nation has come up against her from the north, which will make her land a desolation, and there will be no one to dwell in her, from man to beast; and they have moved and gone away.
verses.50:4: In those days and at that time," says the Lord, "the sons of Israel will come, they and the sons of Judah together; walking and weeping they will hasten, and they will seek the Lord their God.
verses.50:5: They will ask the way to Zion, their faces turned here; they will come and be joined to the Lord in an everlasting covenant that will not be blotted out by any forgetfulness.
verses.50:6: My people have become a lost flock; their shepherds have led them astray and made them wander on the mountains; they have passed from mountain to hill; they have forgotten their resting place.
verses.50:7: All who found them devoured them, and their enemies said, 'We have not sinned, because they have sinned against the Lord, the beauty of righteousness, and the hope of their fathers, the Lord.'
verses.50:8: Withdraw from the midst of Babylon, and go out from the land of the Chaldeans, and be like young goats before the flock.
verses.50:9: For look, I am stirring up and will bring against Babylon an assembly of great nations from the land of the north, and they will prepare themselves against her, and from there she will be captured; its arrow is like that of a mighty man, a killer; it will not return empty.
verses.50:10: And Chaldea will become plunder; all who lay her waste will be filled," says the Lord.
verses.50:11: "Because you exult and speak great things, plundering My inheritance; because you have been let loose like calves upon the grass, and have bellowed like bulls,
verses.50:12: your mother has been greatly put to shame, and she who bore you has been leveled to the dust; look, she will be the last among the nations, deserted, trackless, and parched.
verses.50:13: Because of the wrath of the Lord she will not be inhabited, but she will be reduced entirely to a desolation; everyone who passes through Babylon will be appalled and will hiss over all her plagues.
verses.50:14: Prepare yourselves against Babylon all around, all you who bend the bow; attack her, do not spare the arrows, for she has sinned against the Lord.
verses.50:15: Shout against her; everywhere she has given her hand; her foundations have fallen, her walls have been destroyed, for it is the vengeance of the Lord; take vengeance on her; just as she has done, do to her.
verses.50:16: Destroy the sower from Babylon, and the one holding the sickle in the time of harvest; from the face of the sword of the dove, each one will turn to his own people, and every individual will flee to his own land.
verses.50:17: Israel is a scattered flock; lions have driven him out. First, the king of Assyria devoured him; this last one, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, has crushed his bones."
verses.50:18: Therefore this is what the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, says: "Look, I will visit the king of Babylon and his land, just as I visited the king of Assyria;
verses.50:19: and I will bring Israel back to his dwelling place; and he will graze on Carmel and Bashan, and on Mount Ephraim and Gilead his soul will be satisfied.
verses.50:20: In those days and at that time," says the Lord, "the iniquity of Israel will be sought, and there will be none, and the sin of Judah, and it will not be found; for I will be merciful to those whom I leave behind.
verses.50:21: Go up against the land of those who rule, and visit upon its inhabitants; destroy and kill what is after them," says the Lord, "and do according to all that I have commanded you.
verses.50:22: The sound of war is in the land, and great destruction.
verses.50:23: How has the hammer of the whole earth been broken and crushed? How has Babylon been turned into a desert among the nations?
verses.50:24: I have ensnared you, and you have been captured, Babylon, and you did not know it; you have been found and seized, because you have provoked the Lord.
verses.50:25: The Lord has opened His treasury and has brought out the vessels of His wrath, for the Lord God of hosts has a work in the land of the Chaldeans.
verses.50:26: Come against her from the farthest borders; open up so that those who trample her may come out; lift stones from the road and gather them into heaps; and kill her, and let nothing remain.
verses.50:27: Destroy all her mighty men; let them go down to the slaughter; woe to them, for their day has come, the time of their visitation!"
verses.50:28: The voice of those fleeing and of those who have escaped from the land of Babylon, to declare in Zion the vengeance of the Lord our God, the vengeance of His temple.
verses.50:29: "Declare against Babylon to very many, to all who bend the bow; take your stand against her all around, and let no one escape; repay her according to her work; according to all that she has done, do to her, for she has lifted herself up against the Lord, against the Holy One of Israel.
verses.50:30: Therefore her young men will fall in her streets, and all her men of war will fall silent on that day," says the Lord.
verses.50:31: "Look, I am against you, proud one!" says the Lord God of hosts, "for your day has come, the time of your visitation.
verses.50:32: And the proud one will fall and collapse, and there will be no one to raise him up; and I will kindle a fire in his cities, and it will devour all things around him."
verses.50:33: This is what the Lord of hosts says: "The sons of Israel and the sons of Judah together endure oppression; all who captured them hold them fast; they refuse to let them go.
verses.50:34: Their Redeemer is mighty; the Lord of hosts is His name; in judgment He will defend their cause, so that He may terrify the earth and shake the inhabitants of Babylon.
verses.50:35: A sword against the Chaldeans," says the Lord, "and against the inhabitants of Babylon, and against the princes, and against her wise men.
verses.50:36: A sword against her diviners, who will become fools; a sword against her mighty men, who will be afraid.
verses.50:37: A sword against her horses and against her chariots, and against all the multitude that is in her midst, and they will become like women; a sword against her treasures, which will be plundered.
verses.50:38: A drought will be upon her waters, and they will dry up, for it is a land of carved images, and they boast in portents.
verses.50:39: Therefore dragons will dwell with fig-eating fauns, and ostriches will dwell in her; and she will no longer be inhabited forever, nor will she be built up through generation after generation.
verses.50:40: Just as the Lord overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah and her neighboring cities," says the Lord, "no man will dwell there, and no son of man will inhabit her.
verses.50:41: Look, a people is coming from the north, and a great nation, and many kings will rise up from the ends of the earth.
verses.50:42: They will take hold of bow and shield; they are cruel and merciless; their voice will sound like the sea, and they will mount upon horses, like a man prepared for battle against you, daughter of Babylon.
verses.50:43: The king of Babylon has heard the report of them, and his hands have grown feeble; anguish has seized him, pain like a woman in labor.
verses.50:44: Look, like a lion he will come up from the pride of the Jordan to the strong beauty, for suddenly I will make him run to her. And who will be the chosen one whom I will appoint over her? For who is like Me? And who will withstand Me? And who is this shepherd who can resist My face?"
verses.50:45: Therefore hear the counsel of the Lord which He has conceived in His mind against Babylon, and His thoughts which He has thought concerning the land of the Chaldeans: unless the little ones of the flocks drag them away, unless their dwelling place is destroyed with them.
verses.50:46: At the sound of the captivity of Babylon the earth has been shaken, and an outcry has been heard among the nations.
verses.51:1: This is what the Lord says: "Look, I will stir up against Babylon and against her inhabitants, who have lifted up their heart against Me, as it were a pestilent wind;
verses.51:2: and I will send winnowers into Babylon, and they will winnow her and lay waste her land, for they have come against her from every side on the day of her affliction.
verses.51:3: Let the one who bends his bow not bend it, and let the one in armor not go up; do not spare her young men; put all her army to death.
verses.51:4: And those put to death will fall in the land of the Chaldeans, and the wounded in her regions.
verses.51:5: For Israel and Judah have not been widowed from their God, the Lord of hosts, yet their land is filled with guilt against the Holy One of Israel."
verses.51:6: Flee from the midst of Babylon, and let each one save his own life; do not keep silent about her iniquity, for it is the time of vengeance from the Lord; He Himself will render recompense to her.
verses.51:7: Babylon was a golden cup in the hand of the Lord, intoxicating the whole earth; the nations drank from her wine, and therefore they were shaken.
verses.51:8: Suddenly Babylon has fallen and been shattered. Wail over her; take resin for her pain, if perhaps she may be healed.
verses.51:9: We treated Babylon, and she was not healed; let us abandon her, and let each one go to his own land; for her judgment has reached up to the heavens, and has been lifted up as far as the clouds.
verses.51:10: The Lord has brought forth our justice; come, and let us recount in Zion the work of the Lord our God.
verses.51:11: Sharpen the arrows, fill the quivers; the Lord has stirred up the spirit of the kings of the Medes, and His intent is against Babylon, to destroy her, for it is the vengeance of the Lord, the vengeance of His temple.
verses.51:12: Against the walls of Babylon lift up a standard, increase the watch, post watchmen, prepare ambushes; for the Lord has planned and has done whatever He spoke against the inhabitants of Babylon.
verses.51:13: You who dwell upon many waters, wealthy in treasures, your end has come, the foot-measure of your cutting off.
verses.51:14: The Lord of hosts has sworn by His own life: "Surely I will fill you with men like locusts, and a triumphant chant will be sung over you."
verses.51:15: He who made the earth by His strength prepared the world by His wisdom, and by His understanding stretched out the heavens.
verses.51:16: When He utters His voice, waters are multiplied in the sky; He who lifts up clouds from the end of the earth made lightning for the rain, and brought forth the wind from His treasuries.
verses.51:17: Every man has become foolish apart from knowledge; every metal-caster has been put to shame by a carved image, for their cast work is false, and there is no breath in them.
verses.51:18: The works are empty and worthy of laughter; in the time of their visitation they will perish.
verses.51:19: Not like these is the portion of Jacob, for He Himself is the One who made all things, and Israel is the scepter of His inheritance; the Lord of hosts is His name.
verses.51:20: "You crush weapons of war for Me, and with you I will crush nations, and with you I will destroy kingdoms;
verses.51:21: and with you I will crush the horse and its rider, and with you I will crush the chariot and its rider;
verses.51:22: and with you I will crush man and woman, and with you I will crush old man and boy, and with you I will crush young man and virgin;
verses.51:23: and with you I will crush the shepherd and his flock, and with you I will crush the farmer and his yoked team, and with you I will crush leaders and magistrates;
verses.51:24: and I will pay back to Babylon and to all the inhabitants of Chaldea all their evil that they have done in Zion, before your eyes," says the Lord.
verses.51:25: "Look, I am against you, destructive mountain," says the Lord, "who corrupt the entire earth; and I will stretch out My hand against you, and roll you down from the rocks, and make you a mountain of burning;
verses.51:26: and they will not take from you a stone for a corner, or a stone for foundations; but you will be ruined forever," says the Lord.
verses.51:27: Lift up a standard in the earth, sound the trumpet among the nations, consecrate the nations against her, proclaim against her to the kings of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz; muster Taphsar against her, bring up horses like bristling locusts.
verses.51:28: Consecrate the nations against her, the kings of Media, its leaders and all its magistrates, and the entire land of its dominion.
verses.51:29: And the earth will be shaken and thrown into turmoil, for the plan of the Lord will awaken against Babylon, to make the land of Babylon desolate and uninhabitable.
verses.51:30: The mighty men of Babylon have ceased from battle; they have remained in the strongholds; their strength has been devoured, and they have become like women; her dwellings have been set on fire, her bars have been shattered.
verses.51:31: Runner will come to meet runner, and messenger to meet messenger, to report to the king of Babylon that his city has been captured from one end to the other.
verses.51:32: And the fords have been seized, and the marshes have been set ablaze with fire, and the fighting men have been thrown into turmoil.
verses.51:33: For this is what the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, says: "The daughter of Babylon is like a threshing floor at the time of her threshing; yet a little while, and the time of her harvest will come."
verses.51:34: "Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has eaten me, he has devoured me; he has made me like an empty vessel; he has swallowed me up like a dragon; he has filled his belly with my delicacies, and has cast me out.
verses.51:35: May the iniquity against me and my flesh be upon Babylon," says the dwelling of Zion; "and my blood be upon the inhabitants of Chaldea," says Jerusalem.
verses.51:36: Therefore, this is what the Lord says: "Look, I will judge your cause and exact your vengeance; and I will make her sea desolate, and dry up her spring.
verses.51:37: And Babylon will become heaps, a dwelling of dragons, an astonishment and a hissing, because there is no inhabitant.
verses.51:38: Together they will roar like lions; they will shake out their manes like lion cubs.
verses.51:39: In their heat I will set out their drinks, and I will make them drunk so that they sink into a stupor, and sleep an everlasting sleep, and do not rise," says the Lord.
verses.51:40: "I will bring them down like lambs to the sacrifice, and like rams with young goats.
verses.51:41: How Sheshach has been captured, and the renowned one of the entire earth has been seized! How Babylon has become an astonishment among the nations!
verses.51:42: The sea has come up over Babylon; she has been covered by the multitude of its waves.
verses.51:43: Her cities have become an astonishment, an uninhabitable and desolate land, a land in which no one dwells, nor does a son of man pass through it.
verses.51:44: And I will punish Bel in Babylon, and cast out from his mouth what he had swallowed; and the nations will no longer stream to him, since even the wall of Babylon will collapse."
verses.51:45: Come out from the midst of her, My people, so that each one may save his life from the wrath of the fury of the Lord,
verses.51:46: and so that your heart may not grow faint and you may not fear the report that will be heard in the land; and a report will come in one year, and after this year a report, and wickedness in the land, and ruler over ruler.
verses.51:47: Therefore, look, days are coming, and I will punish the carved images of Babylon, and all her land will be put to shame, and all her slaughtered will fall in the midst of her.
verses.51:48: And the heavens and the earth, and all things that are in them, will offer praise over Babylon, because plunderers will come upon her from the north, says the Lord.
verses.51:49: And just as Babylon caused those killed to fall in Israel, so from Babylon those killed will fall in the entire earth.
verses.51:50: You who have fled the sword, come, do not stand still; remember the Lord from afar, and let Jerusalem come up upon your heart.
verses.51:51: We have been put to shame, for we have heard reproach; disgrace has covered our faces, because foreigners have come upon the sanctuary of the house of the Lord.
verses.51:52: "Therefore, look, the days are coming," says the Lord, "and I will punish her carved images, and throughout all her land the wounded will groan.
verses.51:53: Even if Babylon ascends to heaven and fortifies her strength on high, from Me her devastators will come," says the Lord.
verses.51:54: The sound of an outcry from Babylon, and great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans;
verses.51:55: for the Lord has devastated Babylon, and has destroyed the loud voice from her; and their waves will resound like many waters; their voice has given forth a sound;
verses.51:56: because a plunderer has come against her, that is, against Babylon, and her mighty men have been captured, and their bow has withered; for the Lord is a mighty avenger; He will surely repay.
verses.51:57: "And I will make her princes drunk, and her wise men, and her leaders, and her magistrates, and her mighty men; and they will sleep an everlasting sleep and will not wake up," says the King (the Lord of hosts is His name).
verses.51:58: This is what the Lord of hosts says: "That very broad wall of Babylon will be utterly undermined, and her lofty gates will be burned with fire; and the labors of the peoples will be for nothing, and those of the nations for the fire, and they will utterly perish."
verses.51:59: The word that Jeremiah the prophet commanded Seraiah the son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah, when he went with King Zedekiah to Babylon in the fourth year of his reign; now Seraiah was chief of the prophecy.
verses.51:60: And Jeremiah wrote in one book all the evil that was to come upon Babylon, all these words that are written against Babylon.
verses.51:61: And Jeremiah said to Seraiah: "When you come to Babylon, and see, and read all these words,
verses.51:62: you will say: 'Lord, You have spoken against this place to destroy it, so that there is no one who dwells in it, from man to beast, and so that it becomes a perpetual desolation.'
verses.51:63: And when you have finished reading this book, you will tie a stone to it and throw it into the middle of the Euphrates,
verses.51:64: and you will say: 'Thus Babylon will sink, and will not rise from the face of the affliction that I am bringing upon her, and she will be dissolved.'" Thus far are the words of Jeremiah.
verses.52:1: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
verses.52:2: And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord, according to everything that Jehoiakim had done,
verses.52:3: for the fury of the Lord was against Jerusalem and against Judah, until He cast them away from His presence. And Zedekiah broke away from the king of Babylon.
verses.52:4: Now it happened in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month, that Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came, he and all his army, against Jerusalem; and they besieged it, and built fortifications against it all around.
verses.52:5: And the city was besieged until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
verses.52:6: Then in the fourth month, on the ninth of the month, the famine took hold of the city, and there were no provisions for the people of the land.
verses.52:7: And the city was breached, and all its fighting men fled and went out of the city by night by the way of the gate that is between the two walls and leads to the king's garden, while the Chaldeans were besieging the city all around, and they went away by the way that leads into the wilderness.
verses.52:8: Then the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king, and they seized Zedekiah in the desert that is near Jericho; and all his company scattered from him.
verses.52:9: And when they had captured the king, they brought him to the king of Babylon at Riblah, which is in the land of Hamath, and he spoke judgments to him.
verses.52:10: And the king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and he also killed all the princes of Judah in Riblah.
verses.52:11: And he gouged out the eyes of Zedekiah, and bound him with shackles, and the king of Babylon brought him to Babylon and put him in the prison house until the day of his death.
verses.52:12: Now in the fifth month, on the tenth of the month—which is the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon—Nebuzaradan, commander of the troops, who stood before the king of Babylon, came into Jerusalem,
